vocabulary.meaning: the natural state of rest in which the body and brain recover
examples: Good sleep supports learning and concentration.
Students should not sacrifice sleep every night to study.

vocabulary.meaning: the process by which new memories become more stable after learning
examples: Sleep plays an important role in memory consolidation.
Researchers study memory consolidation after different kinds of learning.
A good night's sleep may improve recall.
The test measured students' recall of new words.

vocabulary.meaning: the ability to keep information in memory over time
examples: Spaced practice improves long-term retention.
Sleep may support the retention of newly learned material.

vocabulary.meaning: a short period of sleep, usually during the day
examples: A short nap helped him feel more alert.
Some studies examine whether a nap improves learning.

vocabulary.meaning: a repeated sequence of stages during sleep
examples: We pass through several sleep cycles each night.
Different parts of the sleep cycle may support different brain functions.

vocabulary.meaning: a stage of sleep associated with slow brain waves and physical recovery
examples: Deep sleep is important for restoration.
Researchers monitor how much deep sleep participants get.

vocabulary.meaning: the act of reviewing material in order to learn or remember it
examples: Do your revision before getting enough sleep, not instead of sleeping.
Short, regular revision sessions can be effective.
Poor sleep can reduce concentration.
Her concentration improved after she changed her sleep routine.

vocabulary.meaning: to gain knowledge or skill through study or experience
examples: People learn more effectively when they are rested.
The experiment tested how sleep affects the ability to learn.
